newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine power firm four-mth net up 35.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine power firm four-mth net up 35.3 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' National Power Corp (Napocor) said on Tuesday it posted a net income of 2.34 billion pesos in the first four months of the year compared with 1.73 billion a year earlier.
Napocor president Guido Alfredo Delgado said in a statement the higher net followed increased energy sales and lower-than-projected operating expenses.
The state-owned power generating firm was expecting a 961 million pesos net income for the period.
Energy sales rose to 11,114 gigawatthour from 10,442 gigawatthours during the period.
"The consistent improvement in our profitability can be attributed in part to the availability of dependable capacity from different types of plants," Delgado said.
Operating expenses were kept at 19.32 billion pesso, lower than the projected level of 23.08 billion pesos.
The lower expenses was due to the shift to cheaper coal and steam to generate power rather than the more expensive diesel.

"This brought down the Napocor's average fuel costs from the year ago figure of 1.10 pesos per kilowatthour to the present 81 centavos per kilowatthour, which in turn generated savings amounting to 309 million pesos," Napocor said.
The company's return on rate base increased to 8.41 percent, up from 7.81 percent in 1996.
